author: ValWood
body:
PMID: 37474791  F6ZE64 LORNRF2
Cell death is a readout here:

The chain the paper supports is: LONRF2 loss → misfolded TDP-43/hnRNP M1 not ubiquitylated and cleared → pTDP-43, G3BP1 and ataxin-2 inclusions accumulate → neurites shorten, neurons look shrunken → TUNEL-positive and neuron counts drop. So yes, the proteostasis failure is upstream and cell death is the endpoint.

What the paper actually shows about cell death is limited to it being a readout:

TUNEL staining was used to measure viability of iPS-cell-derived motor neurons. Lonrf2−/− MNs had lower viability than wild-type after 14 days of culture (FC = 0.39, P < 0.0001), and that was rescued by AAV-delivered FLAG–LONRF2 (FC = 2.65, P < 0.0001).
In vivo, Lonrf2−/− mice showed fewer ChAT-positive and NeuN-positive neurons and more Fluoro-Jade C–positive (degenerating) neurons in spinal cord and cortex at 21 months.
The authors' conclusion is phrased as "loss of LONRF2 in neurons directly causes neuronal cell death and accumulation of misfolded proteins such as pTDP-43."
